item.text: {"text":"GRU4Rec’s BPR-max directly addresses easy-negative dilution: softmax weighting emphasizes high-scoring negatives, with negative-score regularization. The official implementation recommends BPR-max or cross-entropy and supports popularity-controlled sampling plus logQ correction for cross-entropy. These are distinct mechanisms: sampling correction addresses the proposal distribution; it does not identify false negatives. Strong margins against easy sampled items therefore cannot establish precise top-k ranking. [Original paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).\n\nRecent alternatives target informative competitors and sampling bias. RecSys 2024’s Scalable Cross-Entropy approximates full softmax using maximum-inner-product selection of informative outputs; another 2024 study improves sampled WARP/LambdaRank through corrected rank estimates. Neither establishes gains on this pinned Amazon benchmark. [SCE](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26), [rank correction](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/). False-negative work also cautions against treating every plausible competitor as irrelevant: UFNRec uses teacher-generated soft labels, making its complete method unsuitable for this experiment’s strict single-model constraint. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116). Practical hypothesis: compare regularized BPR-max with sampling-corrected sampled softmax within the same GRU4Rec backbone; sweep negative count and hardness, exclude known training positives, and treat additional downweighting of suspected false negatives as an unverified ablation. Select exclusively by official four-category macro validation HR@10, with seeds and training limits fixed."}
